paper_sections.title: Experience dependence of activation in postcentral somatosensory regions
Somatosensory Cortices and IPL Areas in Pain and Action

description.value: The study used fMRI and behavioral experiments to investigate how sensorimotor regions integrate observed hand actions with painful or nonpainful objects, and how observing painful actions biases tactile detection.

spans.text: We used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to demonstrate that postcentral sensorimotor cortex integrates action and object information

description.value: The study included an imaging experiment with repeated within-subject action-by-object conditions, a tactile detection experiment, and auditory and above-threshold control experiments.

spans.text: Each of the 32 action sequences (two actions by eight painful and nonpainful objects) was presented 10 times

definition.value: Painful grasps > neutral grasps, noxious withdrawals, and neutral withdrawals

spans.text: To this end, we contrasted painful grasp trials with trials depicting neutral grasps, neutral withdrawals, and withdrawals from painful objects (painful grasps − 1/3 neutral grasps − 1/3 noxious withdrawal − 1/3 neutral withdrawal).

Whole‐brain random‐effects contrasts were corrected for multiple comparisons, using BrainVoyager's cluster threshold estimator plug‐in, which uses a Monte Carlo simulation procedure (1,000 iterations) to establish the critical cluster size threshold corresponding to a family‐wise alpha of 0.05 corrected for the whole brain.

description.value: Functional MRI data were motion-corrected, spatially smoothed, high-pass filtered, manually coregistered with anatomical T1 scans, resampled to 3 mm isotropic voxels, and transformed to Talairach space.

spans.text: Functional data were motion‐corrected, spatially smoothed with a Gaussian kernel (6 mm FWHM, full width half‐maximum), and low‐frequency drifts were removed with a temporal high‐pass filter (0.006 Hz). Functional data were manually coregistered with 3D anatomical T1 scans (1 × 1 × 1.3 mm  resolution) and then resampled to isometric 3 × 3 × 3 mm  voxels with trilinear interpolation. The 3D scans were transformed into Talairach space
